 Batting key to ending Proteas jinx
 Published : 15 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 15 November 2026, 10:06
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 PHOTO: BCB 
 Bangladesh’s batting will be under the microscope when the visitors face South Africa in the opening Test of the two-match series at Johannesburg’s Wanderers Stadium today. 
 Despite a formidable pace attack that has brought them success at home and abroad -- most recently in Darwin against Australia a few months ago -- the Tigers remain vulnerable with the bat.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Their recent 1-0 home series defeat to West Indies exposed the problem. Bangladesh were bowled out for 272 and 142 in Mirpur, losing the first Test by nine wickets, while Tawhid Hridoy’s unbeaten 242 and 82 in Sylhet helped them salvage a draw in the second.
 Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto said in the pre-match presser that Bangladesh were considering an extra batter but had yet to decide between that option and a second spinner, with the pitch likely to dictate the final combination.
 He reckons that “three pacers will definitely be in the team” alongside a spinner in Bangladesh’s maiden Test at the Wanderers, with Mehidy Hasan Miraz’s recent performances in Australia strengthening the case for spin.
 Shanto said the entire batting unit needed to deliver, particularly those who “get set at the crease”. A big first-innings total, he added, would give Bangladesh’s bowlers a chance to compete as the Tigers aim for their first win over the Proteas in the longest format.
 Read more Shanto urges batting unit to step up against Proteas amid praise for pace attack 
 South Africa, meanwhile, have named four fast bowlers and a spinner in a pace-heavy eleven. Zubayr Hamza returns to address their troublesome No. 3 position, while veteran pacer Dane Paterson also comes in. David Bedingham and Gerald Coetzee make way from the Proteas who beat Australia by 176 runs to clinch their preceding series 2-1.
 Skipper Temba Bavuma said Hamza “scored runs in domestic cricket in all the formats” and more aggressive approach had earned him a recall. Paterson, meanwhile, offered greater variety and a different challenge for batters.
 “He comes with a little bit more skill with the ball, a different kind of challenge for the batters. It's a case of who we felt was the better bowler for these conditions,” Bavuma added.
 Highlights  
 **Bangladesh are set to play a Test at Johannesburg’s Wanderers Stadium for the first time.
 **They have lost all eight Tests in South Africa, five by an innings. Overall, they have lost 14 of their 16 Tests against the Proteas, with the other two ending in rain-affected draws.
 **The two-match series will form part of the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) cycle. Reigning champions South Africa are second in the standings with 71.43 percentage points, while Bangladesh are fifth with 45.83.
 **Bangladesh beat Australia and New Zealand on their most recent Test tours, in 2026 and 2022 respectively. However, they are yet to win a Test away to either South Africa or England among the SENA nations.
